raw.content_en: The US Department of Commerce (BIS) rescinded the Biden-era firearms rule, restoring prior export control treatment for civilian firearms, ammunition, and parts. This reduces licensing burdens for certain semi-automatic firearms and related components previously moved to stricter controls. Exporters must still classify goods under the correct ECCN or EAR99, verify the destination country, and screen all parties against the Entity List, Denied Persons List, and OFAC sanctions. Section 301 tariffs and US HTS alignment remain relevant for outbound and re-export documentation. Firearms exports to certain destinations may still require a DSP-5 or BIS license depending on end use and end user.
raw.content_zh: 美国商务部（BIS）撤销了拜登时期的枪支出口规则，恢复了对民用枪支、弹药及零部件的原有出口管制待遇。此前被收紧管制的部分半自动枪支及相关部件，其许可负担有所降低。出口商仍须按正确的ECCN或EAR99进行归类，核实目的地国家，并对所有交易方进行实体清单、被拒绝人员名单及OFAC制裁筛查。第301条关税及美国HTS编码对齐在出口和再出口单证中仍然重要。根据最终用途和最终用户，向特定目的地出口枪支可能仍需DSP-5或BIS许可。

checklist.desc: Re-classify firearms, ammunition, and parts under the revised rule; confirm whether items fall under ECCN 0A501/0A502 or EAR99 and document the technical basis.
Screen all customers, consignees, and end users against the BIS Entity List, Denied Persons List, Unverified List, and OFAC SDN; retain screening records.
Map the 10-digit HTS line for firearms and parts, check Section 301 additional duty exposure, and document country of origin and value build-up.
Determine whether a BIS license or State Department DSP-5 is required for the destination and end use; prepare end-user and end-use statements.
Verify destination-country firearms import permits, proof marks, and safety certification requirements before shipment.
